title: A finite locally free graded tail gives flat homogeneous chart rings
statement: Let $U$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\mathcal A=\bigoplus_{d\geq0}\mathcal A_d$ a quasi-coherent commutative graded $\mathcal O_U$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures, def-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra]. Fix $m\geq0$ and suppose that every $\mathcal A_d$, $d\geq m$, is finite locally free: every point has an open neighbourhood on which that sheaf is a finite direct sum of copies of $\mathcal O_U$ [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]. No common neighbourhood trivializing all degrees is assumed. For any affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq U$, put $A_d=\Gamma(V,\mathcal A_d)$ and $A=\bigoplus_{d\geq0}A_d$, with the induced graded multiplication. Fix any $f\in A_1$ and put $C=A_{(f),0}$ [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero]. Each $A_d$ for $d\geq m$ is a finitely presented projective $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] and is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. On the small nonempty directed set $\{d\in\mathbf N:d\geq m\}$ consider the $R$-modules $A_d$, with transition $A_d\to A_e$, $a\mapsto f^{e-d}a$ for $e\geq d$. The maps $\mu_d:A_d\to C$, $a\mapsto a/f^d$, exhibit $C$ as their colimit in $R$-modules [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. More explicitly, for every $R$-module $M$ and compatible family of linear maps $h_d:A_d\to M$, there is a unique linear $h:C\to M$ with $h\mu_d=h_d$; for $a\in A_e$, $e\geq0$, and any $D\geq\max(e,m)$ it satisfies $h(a/f^e)=h_D(f^{D-e}a)$. Consequently $C$ is a flat $R$-module. These conclusions hold for $f=0$ and nilpotent $f$ and impose no equality $A_0=R$, regularity of $f$, polynomial presentation, or Noetherian hypothesis on $U$.

proof.text: For each $d\geq m$, apply lem-pc-finite-flat-affine-sections-projective to $\mathcal A_d$ and the affine open $V$. It gives finite presentation and projectivity of $A_d$ over $R$. Apply lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat to obtain flatness. This is a separate application for each degree; no simultaneous trivialization is used.

source.place: Tag 051G (lemma-local-artinian-characterize-flat), first sentence of proof, for projective implies flat; affine sections supplied by the cited project theorem

proof.text: Put $I=\{d\in\mathbf N:d\geq m\}$. It is small, contains $m$, and has upper bound $\max(d,e)$ for each pair. Graded bilinearity makes $t_{de}(a)=f^{e-d}a$ linear; $t_{dd}=1$ and $t_{eh}t_{de}=t_{dh}$ follow by adding exponents. The fraction operations make $\mu_d(a)=a/f^d$ linear, and $\mu_et_{de}=\mu_d$. Every $a/f^e\in C$ equals $\mu_D(f^{D-e}a)$ for any $D\geq\max(e,m)$.

source.place: Tag 00JM (section-proj), equal-degree fractions; Tag 00CO (definition-localization), fraction operations

proof.text: Given compatible linear maps $h_d:A_d\to M$, prescribe $h(a/f^e)=h_D(f^{D-e}a)$ for $D\geq\max(e,m)$. Enlarging $D$ does not change this value by compatibility, so any two choices agree at their maximum. If $a/f^e=b/f^t$, the localization relation gives $k\geq0$ with $f^k(f^ta-f^eb)=0$. Choose $L\geq\max(m,D,E,e+t+k)$, where $D,E$ are the chosen levels. Multiplication by $f^{L-e-t-k}$ gives $f^{L-e}a=f^{L-t}b$ in $A_L$. Applying $h_L$ and compatibility proves equality of the prescribed values. Thus $h$ is well-defined without cancellation.

source.place: Tag 00CO (definition-localization), equality relation, specialized to powers of f; explicit agent common-degree calculation

proof.text: For two fractions choose $D\geq\max(e,t,m)$ and set $u=f^{D-e}a$, $v=f^{D-t}b$. Then $a/f^e+b/f^t=(u+v)/f^D$, so linearity of $h_D$ gives additivity of $h$. For $r\in R$, $r(a/f^e)=(ra)/f^e$ gives $h(r(a/f^e))=rh(a/f^e)$; also $h(0)=0$. Taking $D=d$ gives $h\mu_d=h_d$. Any map with these identities has the same value on every $a/f^e=\mu_D(f^{D-e}a)$, so it equals $h$. This proves exactly the colimit universal property and its stated formula.

source.place: Tags 00CO (definition-localization) and 002F (categories-definition-colimit); explicit linearity and uniqueness calculation

proof.text: The diagram of step 2 is indexed by a small nonempty directed set, all its modules are flat by step 1, and steps 3--4 prove that its cocone with vertex $C$ is a colimit. Apply lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-flat-modules to this cocone to conclude that $C$ is flat over $R$.

If $f^N=0$, every localization fraction is zero. Every compatible family also satisfies $h_d(a)=h_{d+N}(f^Na)=0$, so the same universal property gives the zero module, which is flat by step 5. This includes $f=0$, the zero ring and empty affine opens. All calculations use only the structural action $R\to A_0$ and the degree-one condition on $f$; they require no injectivity, regularity or Noetherian hypothesis.

lean.statement: theorem locallyFree_tail_chart_flatness {X : Scheme.{u}} (A : RelativeProjAlgebra X) (m : ℕ) (htail : ∀ d : ℕ, m ≤ d → (A.piece d).IsFiniteLocallyFree) (V : X.affineOpens) (f : A.grade V 1) : (∀ d : ℕ, m ≤ d → Module.FinitePresentation Γ(X, V.1) Γ(A.piece d, V.1) ∧ Module.Projective Γ(X, V.1) Γ(A.piece d, V.1) ∧ Module.Flat Γ(X, V.1) Γ(A.piece d, V.1)) ∧ (∃ (t : ∀ (d e : ℕ), d ≤ e → Γ(A.piece d, V.1) →ₗ[Γ(X, V.1)] Γ(A.piece e, V.1)) (μ : ∀ d : ℕ, Γ(A.piece d, V.1) →ₗ[Γ(X, V.1)] A.tailChartRing V f), (∀ (d e : ℕ) (hde : d ≤ e) (a : Γ(A.piece d, V.1)), (A.tailChartSection V e (t d e hde a)).val = f.val ^ (e - d) * (A.tailChartSection V d a).val) ∧ (∀ (d : ℕ) (a : Γ(A.piece d, V.1)), μ d a = A.tailChartFraction V f d a) ∧ (∀ (d : ℕ) (hd : m ≤ d), t d d le_rfl = LinearMap.id) ∧ (∀ (d e k : ℕ) (hd : m ≤ d) (hde : d ≤ e) (hek : e ≤ k), (t e k hek).comp (t d e hde) = t d k (hde.trans hek)) ∧ (∀ (d e : ℕ) (hd : m ≤ d) (hde : d ≤ e), (μ e).comp (t d e hde) = μ d) ∧ (∀ (M : Type (max u v)) [AddCommGroup M] [Module Γ(X, V.1) M] (h : ∀ d : {d : ℕ // m ≤ d}, Γ(A.piece d.val, V.1) →ₗ[Γ(X, V.1)] M), (∀ (d e : {d : ℕ // m ≤ d}) (hde : d.val ≤ e.val), (h e).comp (t d.val e.val hde) = h d) → ∃ H : A.tailChartRing V f →ₗ[Γ(X, V.1)] M, (∀ d : {d : ℕ // m ≤ d}, H.comp (μ d.val) = h d) ∧ (∀ H' : A.tailChartRing V f →ₗ[Γ(X, V.1)] M, (∀ d : {d : ℕ // m ≤ d}, H'.comp (μ d.val) = h d) → H' = H) ∧ (∀ (e : ℕ) (a : Γ(A.piece e, V.1)) (D : ℕ) (heD : e ≤ D) (hmD : m ≤ D), H (A.tailChartFraction V f e a) = h ⟨D, hmD⟩ (t e D heD a)))) ∧ Module.Flat Γ(X, V.1) (A.tailChartRing V f)
